requirements.evidence: Covers the whole contract: migrations with cascades, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:13-26); Queue model with fillable, casts and relations (app/Models/Queue.php:11-37); Entity::queues() (app/Models/Entity.php:46-49); enums; InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException; IssueTicket rejects negative priority, locks the queue row and re-reads is_active inside the transaction, and retries on UniqueConstraintViolationException (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:28-58); write-once enforced in the updating hook (app/Models/Ticket.php:60-71); call() locks the row, authorizes and rejects non-waiting tickets (app/Models/Ticket.php:116-136); the factory allocates or keeps a code and has forQueue (TicketFactory.php:35-48). One gap: nextCode() takes the newest surviving valid code (Ticket.php:91-108), so deleting the last ticket (A003 in A001..A003) makes the next code A003 again. That contradicts 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number', and the docs were narrowed to match ('while a later valid code exists').

conventions.evidence: The domain write is an invokable Action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php). Calling is authorized through a new TicketPolicy (app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php:14-16) via Gate::forUser()->authorize, not inline checks. Migrations have timestamped generator-style names and reversible down(). Fillable is declared deliberately. CHANGELOG [Unreleased], docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and docs/architecture.md (TODO replaced with the test link) are updated in the same change. Model style (casts() method, #[Fillable]) is consistent across the new models.

security.evidence: Ticket::call authorizes on the freshly locked row before any write and leaves the ticket unchanged on denial (Ticket.php:119-125). The policy scopes by $ticket->queue->entity_id. Issuance trusts the DB state and not the passed model (IssueTicket.php:36-43). There is no HTTP/Livewire surface in this change, and I found no mass-assignment or output-escaping concern.

tests.evidence: Tests come before production behaviour for every requirement: defaults, sequence, per-queue codes, explicit priority/channel, inactive and stale-queue rejection with nothing persisted, negative priority (IssueTicketTest.php); A999->A1000->A1001, malformed codes, middle deletion, factory explicit code and forQueue, write-once (TicketModelTest.php); single call, all roles, a non-member, a member of another entity and a repeat call leaving the ticket unchanged (TicketCallTest.php); schema and indexes (TicketSchemaTest.php). Gaps: the collision-retry path is never exercised. The 'ticket defaults ... enforced by the database' test inserts through the factory, which sets those values explicitly, so it does not test DB defaults. The entity->queue cascade named in the test title is not checked (TicketSchemaTest.php:66-85).

simplicity.evidence: Lean and direct: no service layer, a single MUTABLE_AFTER_ISSUANCE list with array_diff on getDirty(), and a small retry loop. nextCode() plucks every code in the queue on each issuance (Ticket.php:93-96) when only the newest valid one is needed. That is fine at MVP scale but grows linearly with queue history.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are small and PHPDoc on public methods explains the insertion-order rule. A minor leftover: TicketSchemaTest.php:79-84 creates an unused $user and asserts `$user->id` is not null, which tests nothing.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, enums, exception, action, policy, factories, migrations, tests and the doc/CHANGELOG updates the task and conventions require. No HTTP, Livewire, call-next selection or cancellation was added.

issues.explanation: nextCode() uses the latest surviving valid code, so deleting the most recently issued ticket lets its number be reused, contrary to 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'. The docs were narrowed (docs/business-rules.md, 'while a later valid code exists') instead of the rule being met.

The test claims to check DB defaults and the queue/entity cascades, but the factory sets the default values explicitly and only the queue->ticket cascade is exercised. It also contains a meaningless $user assertion.
The retry on a unique (queue_id, code) collision and the final RuntimeException after five attempts have no test.
pluck('code') loads the queue's entire code history on every issuance. Iterating lazily, or limiting the query, would avoid linear growth.

review.summary: The change adds the queue/ticket persistence, models, enums, factories, the IssueTicket action with a locked DB-state check and collision retry, write-once enforcement and a policy-authorized single call, with thorough Pest tests and synced docs. It meets nearly the whole contract and the conventions; the main defects are code reuse when the last ticket is deleted (and the docs being softened to match) and a few weak or missing tests. Approve with small fixes.
